controls.title: Confirm test scope, authority, and safety boundaries
controls.applicability: Every audit, including internal applications.
controls.verify: Before active testing, record asset owner authorization, exact environments and targets, allowed techniques, dates, bounded request/concurrency limits, test identities, exclusions, rollback owner, and stop contacts. Default to local/staging with synthetic data. Explicitly scope and approve production or destructive/availability-impacting tests separately.
controls.pass: A reviewable authorization record covers the proposed work. Unapproved tests stay Blocked; no real-secret collection, exfiltration, live-card charges, unsolicited messages, real-account brute force, or production load tests occur. Stop on unexpected data, instability, or out-of-scope effects.
controls.evidence: Scope record with approver, target list, limits, stop/rollback procedure, and blocked-test log; redact credentials.

controls.title: Freeze the release baseline and exposed surface
controls.applicability: Every release candidate or security-relevant change.
controls.verify: Reconcile source routes, deployment manifests, API specifications, scheduled jobs, admin consoles, integrations, and client builds. Record commit/build, runtime/framework versions, environment configuration, domains, and externally reachable entry points from existing inventory; do not discover or probe unrelated hosts.
controls.pass: The inventory names owners and exposure for all observed entry points, including old API versions and internal/admin paths. Differences between reviewed build, staging, and intended production configuration are explicit and assigned for verification.
controls.evidence: Versioned asset/route inventory and build identifier; reviewed configuration diff without secret values.

controls.title: Map sensitive assets, data flows, and trust boundaries
controls.applicability: Every app processing identities, business records, files, payments, or third-party data.
controls.verify: Trace a synthetic request from browser through edge, application, database/storage, queues, workers, and integrations. Mark tenant boundaries, external inputs, sensitive stores, credentials, encryption boundaries, and who may read or modify each asset.
controls.pass: An owner-reviewed diagram and data inventory identify each trust crossing and its validation, identity, authorization, retention, and encryption responsibility; no component is trusted merely because it is internal.
controls.evidence: Dated data-flow diagram and asset-to-control map covering the release's critical workflows.

controls.title: Model adversaries and business abuse cases
controls.applicability: Every app; focus on workflows with money, scarce inventory, privileged actions, or private records.
controls.verify: Walk through misuse by an anonymous caller, ordinary user, other tenant, compromised administrator, and compromised integration. For checkout, bookings, auctions, and account changes, write the invariants that must hold across retries, failures, and concurrency.
controls.pass: Plausible attack paths and impact are linked to concrete test cases, responsible owners, and controls. High-impact scenarios receive manual review beyond scanner coverage, and security-relevant changes update the model.
controls.evidence: Threat scenarios with preconditions, affected assets, impact, mitigations, and mapped test IDs.

controls.title: Determine coverage and justify exclusions
controls.applicability: Every audit.
controls.verify: Review every checklist control against the actual architecture and selected ASVS assurance target. Record applicable, not applicable with architectural evidence, or applicability unresolved. Add stack/business-specific requirements and current advisory checks rather than assuming this catalog is exhaustive.
controls.pass: No check defaults to Pass or Not applicable. Missing access, unsupported tooling, or a test being unsafe is Blocked/Untested with an owner, not an exclusion. ASVS conformance is claimed only with a complete versioned requirement mapping and evidence.
controls.evidence: Coverage matrix, explicit exclusions, additional controls, selected standards/versions, and unresolved-scope list.

controls.title: Require reproducible findings and an honest release decision
controls.applicability: Every readiness recommendation.
controls.verify: For each finding preserve sanitized steps, expected/actual outcome, exact build, impact, finding severity rationale, fix and retest. Reconcile evidence and applicability before human review; keep all unresolved Critical/High findings, accepted risks at those severities and applicable untested/blocked Critical/High checks visible.
controls.pass: No ordinary production-ready recommendation is issued with unresolved Critical/High findings (including accepted risks), applicable untested/blocked Critical/High checks, unresolved applicability or missing scope/evidence. Lower-risk acceptance names an accountable owner, rationale, compensating controls, expiry and retest. Scan success never proves perfect security.
controls.evidence: Findings register, retest results, named risk decisions, remaining limitations, and release decision tied to the exact build.

controls.title: Enforce authentication on every protected entry point
controls.applicability: Apps with protected pages, APIs, administrative tools, or service endpoints.
controls.verify: Using local/staging routes, request each protected action without credentials, with invalid credentials, and with a disabled test identity. Include alternate verbs, legacy routes, direct API calls, debug/demo modes, and fallback identity-provider failures.
controls.pass: Every protected operation rejects unauthenticated/disabled callers without returning private data or causing a side effect. Authentication failures fail closed; no production default, demo, or shared administrator login remains.
controls.evidence: Route/identity test matrix with sanitized responses and side-effect assertions; relevant guard configuration.

controls.title: Apply a defensible password policy
controls.applicability: Locally managed password authentication; review provider policy if delegated.
controls.verify: In a test account, try a known-common password, a long passphrase, spaces/Unicode, and boundary lengths. Inspect blocklist, minimum/maximum handling, password-manager support, and recovery parity. Compare the chosen assurance policy with current NIST guidance.
controls.pass: Common/compromised passwords are rejected; long passphrases and password managers work without silent truncation. Length and throttling match the documented assurance target; arbitrary composition or periodic rotation is not substituted for compromise-driven controls.
controls.evidence: Policy and provider settings, boundary test outcomes, and reference version; never retain test password values.

controls.title: Use adaptive salted password hashing
controls.applicability: Any component storing passwords or reusable password verifiers.
controls.verify: Review hashing library and configured algorithm/cost. Create two synthetic accounts with the same disposable password and inspect only their synthetic stored verifiers. Verify legacy-hash upgrade behavior and benchmark within the agreed local resource budget.
controls.pass: No plaintext, reversible password storage or fast unsalted hash is used. Maintained adaptive hashing with unique salts and current recommended parameters is configured; alternatives need documented platform constraints and security review. Weak active verifiers remain an unresolved finding until remediated or invalidated: a migration plan alone is not a pass. Rehash/reset migration and rollback behavior are verified.
controls.evidence: Algorithm and cost configuration, synthetic salt comparison, migration test, and bounded timing results; no real hashes copied.

controls.title: Constrain login guessing and account enumeration
controls.applicability: Login, registration, recovery, invitation lookup, and OTP endpoints.
controls.verify: Compare a small authorized sample of existing/nonexistent synthetic accounts for body, status and timing differences. Inspect per-account and network/device throttling, lockout recovery and bypass routes; use configured low test thresholds rather than guessing real accounts.
controls.pass: Responses do not unnecessarily disclose account existence. Server-side limits apply across equivalent endpoints without allowing a trivial permanent victim lockout; recovery and alerting are available. CAPTCHA alone is not the control.
controls.evidence: Sanitized comparison results, limiter settings and bounded threshold test showing enforcement.

controls.title: Enforce MFA and step-up authentication consistently
controls.applicability: Privileged accounts, sensitive actions, or any product claiming MFA protection.
controls.verify: With a test identity, complete only the first factor and call APIs directly. Try alternate login/recovery routes, remembered sessions and factor enrollment/removal. Review whether high-impact administrator access has a phishing-resistant option.
controls.pass: Required second-factor/step-up checks are enforced server-side before privileged work. Factor changes require recent strong authentication and user notification; password-only fallbacks cannot silently bypass the documented assurance policy.
controls.evidence: Factor-state/action matrix, provider settings and synthetic notification evidence.

controls.title: Protect OTPs, recovery codes, and MFA reset
controls.applicability: OTP, backup codes, device replacement, or support-assisted MFA reset.
controls.verify: Use synthetic factors to retry one already-used code, an expired code, and a code for another account/session. Inspect attempt ceilings, recovery-code storage, reset identity proof, and support tooling. Route all notifications to a test sink.
controls.pass: Codes are short-lived, scoped, rate-limited, and one-use where required. Recovery does not reduce assurance to public information or security questions; reset paths are authorized, logged, and notify the account owner.
controls.evidence: Replay/expiry/cross-account results, redacted recovery procedure and test notification log.

controls.title: Make password reset and magic links single-use and account-bound
controls.applicability: Password reset, passwordless email links, or account activation tokens.
controls.verify: In local/staging with a mail sink, exercise expiry, reuse, cancellation, cross-account substitution and two concurrent redemptions. Inspect token generation/storage, URL construction, rate limits and post-reset session handling; change only owned synthetic accounts.
controls.pass: Unpredictable, scoped tokens expire and are consumed atomically. Trusted configuration builds the reset origin, tokens do not leak to analytics/referrers/logs, and the account cannot be changed before valid redemption. Session revocation follows the documented compromise policy.
controls.evidence: Token lifecycle tests, synthetic mail template, storage design and session invalidation result without live tokens.

controls.title: Bind invitations to intended tenant, identity, and privilege
controls.applicability: Invite-only registration, staff onboarding, sharing, or tenant membership invitations.
controls.verify: Create two test tenants and invite an owned test address. Attempt reuse, expiry, revocation, concurrent acceptance, recipient/tenant/role modification, and acceptance after the inviter loses authority. Inspect token entropy, storage and delivery limits.
controls.pass: Only an authorized inviter can grant permitted roles. Redemption verifies intended identity/tenant, immutable server-side grants, expiry and revocation, and consumes a token once. Invitation possession alone cannot silently elevate or link an unrelated account.
controls.evidence: Invitation state/role matrix, bounded negative tests and grant record before/after redemption.

controls.title: Protect email changes and federated account linking
controls.applicability: Email-as-identity, account linking, identity-provider federation, or account merge.
controls.verify: Using owned identities, attempt to change email or attach a provider without recent authentication, with an unverified email, with a recycled/duplicate email, or from another provider subject. Test old/new address verification and notifications through a test sink.
controls.pass: Sensitive identity changes require appropriate reauthentication and verification. Stable provider issuer/subject identifies federated accounts; matching an unverified email does not prove ownership. Linking/merging cannot transfer another user's data or privileges.
controls.evidence: Identity-link policy, provider claim mapping, account-change negative tests and notification results.

controls.title: Scope and protect session cookies
controls.applicability: Cookie-based sessions or authentication cookies.
controls.verify: Inspect actual Set-Cookie values from local/staging HTTPS login, refresh and logout. Review Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, expiry and prefix choices; check sibling-subdomain assumptions and intentional cross-site flows.
controls.pass: Authentication cookies are Secure and HttpOnly, have least necessary scope and suitable SameSite behavior, and are cleared using matching scope. Broad parent-domain sharing has an explicit trust justification; SameSite is not treated as complete CSRF protection.
controls.evidence: Redacted header captures and cookie-scope rationale including cross-site flow tests.

controls.title: Prevent session fixation and rotate privilege transitions
controls.applicability: Stateful sessions or tokens reused across authentication/privilege changes.
controls.verify: Set a pre-login synthetic session, then log in or elevate privilege and compare identifiers without recording full secrets. Attempt the old session against a protected fixture; inspect whether URL/query session identifiers are accepted.
controls.pass: Authentication and privilege elevation issue a fresh session; the previous low-assurance identifier cannot access the elevated session. Session identifiers are generated cryptographically, not user-controlled, and are not accepted from URLs.
controls.evidence: Lifecycle assertions using token fingerprints, guard code locations and accepted credential-channel configuration.

controls.title: Enforce idle, absolute, and revocation limits on sessions
controls.applicability: Authenticated sessions, persistent login, and refresh mechanisms.
controls.verify: Use a controlled clock or short local lifetimes to test idle/absolute expiry, logout, password reset, disabled accounts and privilege removal. Replay only synthetic credentials and inspect all nodes/caches that participate in revocation.
controls.pass: Server-side limits match the documented risk-based session policy. Logout/revocation prevents further protected use within an explicit maximum delay, including other workers and refresh routes; extending client cookie expiry cannot extend server authorization.
controls.evidence: Configured durations, clock-based tests, multi-node revocation results and documented residual lifetime.

controls.title: Validate JWT signatures, keys, claims, and token purpose
controls.applicability: JWT access tokens, ID tokens, signed invitation tokens, or JWT sessions.
controls.verify: Against a local verifier, use synthetic tokens with a changed signature, disallowed/none algorithm, wrong issuer/audience/type, unknown key ID, expired/not-yet-valid timestamps and missing required claims. Inspect key selection and any remote key discovery.
controls.pass: A maintained verifier pins allowed algorithms and trusted issuer/key sources, validates signature and required claims with bounded clock skew, and rejects token-type confusion. Token-supplied key URLs cannot redirect trust; decoding a JWT is not verification.
controls.evidence: Verifier configuration and negative-token unit/integration results with no real signing keys or bearer tokens.

controls.title: Limit token lifetimes and detect refresh-token replay
controls.applicability: Access/refresh tokens, especially long-lived browser or mobile sessions.
controls.verify: Record access/refresh lifetime and maximum authorization staleness. In a synthetic session, rotate or sender-constrain refresh tokens, replay the old token, revoke the account, rotate signing keys and test the permitted overlap window.
controls.pass: Lifetimes are justified by impact and revocation capability. Refresh tokens are protected and bound to the client/session; rotation with reuse handling or sender constraint prevents unlimited replay. Scope cannot expand during refresh, and key rollover does not indefinitely retain compromised trust.
controls.evidence: Lifetime/revocation policy, replay and scope tests, and key-rotation simulation with identifiers only.

controls.title: Bind OAuth/OIDC callbacks to the initiating login
controls.applicability: OAuth authorization or OpenID Connect sign-in.
controls.verify: Use a test identity provider to alter redirect URI, state, PKCE verifier, issuer, nonce where applicable and authorization code. Test code reuse, cross-session callback and account linking; inspect configured grants and client secrets.
controls.pass: Authorization-code flows use appropriate PKCE and request binding, strict registered redirects and verified provider/token claims. Replayed or mismatched callbacks fail. Deprecated implicit/resource-owner-password flows are absent unless a reviewed migration exception remains a finding; OAuth alone is not identity proof.
controls.evidence: Provider/client configuration, callback negative tests and maintained-library/version record.

controls.title: Validate SAML assertions and replay protection
controls.applicability: SAML single sign-on.
controls.verify: With an isolated test IdP and maintained SAML library, test unsigned/tampered assertions, wrong audience/destination/recipient, expired timestamps, replay, request mismatch and duplicate/wrapped assertion fixtures. Inspect trusted metadata and signing-key rollover.
controls.pass: Only the validated signed assertion supplies identity/roles; issuer, audience, recipient, time and request binding are enforced. Replays fail. Unsolicited SSO, if enabled, has explicit compensating controls and no arbitrary account-linking path.
controls.evidence: SAML validation settings, trusted metadata fingerprint and synthetic invalid-assertion results.

controls.title: Validate passkey registration and authentication ceremonies
controls.applicability: WebAuthn/passkey or security-key authentication.
controls.verify: With a virtual authenticator or owned test key, test expired/replayed challenge, wrong origin/RP ID, unexpected credential/account binding, and missing required user verification. Test adding/removing a credential from a stale session and recovery fallback.
controls.pass: A maintained server library validates challenge, origin, RP ID, signature, credential ownership and required flags. Registration needs an authorized account context; credential changes require recent authentication. Recovery preserves the chosen assurance level.
controls.evidence: Ceremony configuration and virtual-authenticator negative tests; credential identifiers redacted.

controls.title: Define default-deny authorization for each action
controls.applicability: Any protected data or action, including internal tools.
controls.verify: Build an actor × resource × action matrix for anonymous, ordinary, privileged, service and suspended identities. Review server policy enforcement and test omitted/unknown roles and policy-service errors with synthetic fixtures.
controls.pass: Every sensitive operation has an explicit policy and defaults to denial. UI hiding, network location, UUIDs, or authentication alone do not authorize access; authorization errors fail closed without partial mutations.
controls.evidence: Reviewed permission matrix, enforcement locations and denied-action/side-effect assertions.

controls.title: Check object ownership on every read and write
controls.applicability: Endpoints accepting object IDs, slugs, filenames, or nested resource identifiers.
controls.verify: Create resources owned by two test users. As each identity, substitute the other's identifier in path, query, body and nested/batch inputs for read, update, delete, download and workflow actions. Test one permitted and one denied object per path.
controls.pass: The server authorizes the actual object/action for the current caller on every access. Unpredictable IDs are not the defense; denial returns no private fields and causes no unauthorized state change.
controls.evidence: Two-identity object/action matrix, sanitized requests and database/queue side-effect checks.

controls.title: Derive tenant context from verified membership
controls.applicability: Multi-tenant or multi-organization applications.
controls.verify: Use two owned test tenants and alter tenant selectors in hosts, headers, paths, cookies and request bodies. Check database queries/RLS roles, cache keys, file storage and queue messages; run sequential tests with pooled connections for tenant-context leakage.
controls.pass: Selectors never establish membership. Verified server context scopes every data access, pooled context resets correctly, and caches/storage/workers preserve isolation. Cross-tenant reads, writes and administrative transitions fail.
controls.evidence: Tenant-isolation tests, query/policy excerpts and cache/storage/queue context map.

controls.title: Enforce function and privilege boundaries
controls.applicability: Administrative functions or different user roles.
controls.verify: Call privileged endpoints directly with ordinary and service test identities, including alternate methods, legacy versions, hidden UI actions, exports, approval/refund actions and role assignment. Test a legitimate privileged call as a control.
controls.pass: Each action enforces required privilege server-side and cannot be reached by method/route variants. A user cannot grant roles beyond their authority or approve their own request where separation of duties is required.
controls.evidence: Role/action negative tests, actual side effects and policy rules.

controls.title: Authorize individual fields and prevent mass assignment
controls.applicability: Object binding, serializers, profile/order updates, PATCH, GraphQL inputs or admin forms.
controls.verify: Add protected fields such as role, tenant, owner, price, paid status and approval flags to synthetic create/update requests, including nested structures. Compare returned fields for low-privilege identities and inspect serializer/DTO allowlists.
controls.pass: Only authorized writable fields bind to the model; protected values are server-derived. Responses expose only fields the caller may see. Rejected fields do not change records even when combined with valid changes.
controls.evidence: Field-permission matrix, payload variants, before/after fixture records and serialization configuration.

controls.title: Apply authorization to lists, search, aggregates and exports
controls.applicability: Search/list/filter endpoints, counts, reporting, bulk jobs or downloadable exports.
controls.verify: Populate distinct synthetic data for two users/tenants, then test filters, pagination, totals, autocomplete, aggregates, export creation and download under each identity. Include a mixed authorized/unauthorized bulk request.
controls.pass: Filtering and aggregation occur within the authorized data set, and export/download permissions are rechecked appropriately. Bulk processing cannot leak counts/fields or perform partial unauthorized work; documented existence disclosures are intentional.
controls.evidence: Seeded dataset, expected/actual row and aggregate assertions, export permissions and mixed-batch outcome.

controls.title: Preserve identity through workers and delegated services
controls.applicability: Background jobs, queues, service-to-service calls, scheduled exports or delegated integrations.
controls.verify: Trace a synthetic privileged job from request to worker. Alter the serialized user/tenant/action fields, revoke the requester before execution, and inspect service credential scopes and retry/dead-letter processing in isolated fixtures.
controls.pass: Trusted, validated context and appropriate current authorization reach each worker. A broadly privileged service cannot be used as a confused deputy for an unauthorized caller; retries and delayed jobs retain their permission boundaries.
controls.evidence: Job-context schema, tamper/revocation test results, worker policy and service-scope configuration.

controls.title: Guard Next.js route handlers, Server Actions and data access
controls.applicability: Next.js applications with protected server-rendered data, route handlers, or Server Actions.
controls.verify: Inventory server entry points and call them directly with unauthorized test sessions. Inspect the data access layer and action/handler guards; bypass the client UI and verify that middleware/proxy redirects are not the only access check.
controls.pass: Each server entry point verifies authentication and authorization near protected data/actions. Client components receive only permitted fields; layout-level checks, hidden controls and action identifiers do not substitute for server authorization.
controls.evidence: Route/action matrix, guard code locations and direct-call integration tests for the installed Next.js version.

controls.title: Revoke stale permissions and constrain impersonation
controls.applicability: Role changes, tenant departure, account disabling, support impersonation or delegated administration.
controls.verify: With existing test sessions and queued work, remove membership/privilege and repeat protected actions after the documented propagation interval. Review support impersonation initiation, scope, visible state, audit trail, expiry and exit behavior.
controls.pass: Removed authority cannot persist beyond an explicit bounded interval across tokens, caches and jobs. Impersonation requires a separate authorized action, cannot exceed delegated scope, and records both initiating and effective identities.
controls.evidence: Revocation timing and action results; impersonation policy, logs using synthetic identities and expiry test.

controls.title: Prevent CSRF on browser-authenticated state changes
controls.applicability: Endpoints where browsers automatically attach credentials, including cookie sessions and login/account-link flows.
controls.verify: From a separate local test origin, submit permitted synthetic state-change requests with missing/invalid tokens and simple content types; also test legitimate requests. Inspect framework CSRF, Origin/Referer or Fetch Metadata enforcement and fallback behavior.
controls.pass: Cross-site unauthorized changes fail server-side. State-changing GETs are absent. Defenses fit the credential model and protect all relevant routes; SameSite and CORS alone are not assumed to stop every CSRF path.
controls.evidence: Cross-origin test matrix and before/after state assertions; CSRF and proxy-origin configuration.

controls.title: Evaluate CORS by reachable data and credential exposure
controls.applicability: Browser-accessible endpoints with cross-origin sharing requirements or CORS headers.
controls.verify: In staging, compare allowlisted, untrusted and null origins, credentialed/noncredentialed requests and preflight/actual responses. Test allowlist parsing for near-match hostnames using owned local origins and inspect cache Vary behavior.
controls.pass: Sensitive responses are readable only by explicitly trusted origins when credentials are permitted. Public non-sensitive resources may intentionally allow '*'. CORS is a browser sharing policy, not server authentication; its presence or absence alone is not a vulnerability.
controls.evidence: Origin/credentials/readability matrix, response headers and documented intended cross-origin consumers.

controls.title: Deploy an effective Content Security Policy
controls.applicability: Browser-rendered HTML, especially pages with authenticated or sensitive workflows.
controls.verify: Inspect the enforced response policy on normal/error/auth pages and third-party embeds. In an isolated fixture, attempt one harmless inline script and an unapproved resource; inspect nonce generation, hash coverage, violation reports and known unsafe allowances.
controls.pass: The policy restricts script/object/base and other relevant capabilities using reviewed sources, per-response nonces or hashes as appropriate. Unexpected scripts are blocked and allowed workflows function. Report-only deployment is explicitly recorded; CSP never substitutes for output encoding/sanitization.
controls.evidence: Actual headers, policy rationale, safe browser blocking results and sanitized violation sample.

controls.title: Control framing and protect sensitive confirmations
controls.applicability: Pages with authenticated actions or sensitive user decisions; identify legitimate embedding needs.
controls.verify: Load a staging action page in an iframe on an owned untrusted origin and in each required trusted embed. Inspect response frame-ancestors and compatible legacy controls. Review reauthentication/confirmation for high-impact actions that can also be targeted through separate windows.
controls.pass: Unapproved framing is blocked while approved embeddings retain appropriate restrictions. Frame-busting JavaScript is not the sole control, and clickjacking protections do not replace transaction authorization.
controls.evidence: Frame test results, response policy and sensitive-action confirmation behavior.

controls.title: Set intentional content, referrer and browser capability policies
controls.applicability: HTTP responses rendered or consumed by browsers.
controls.verify: Inspect representative HTML, API, download, error and redirect responses for accurate Content-Type, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and relevant Permissions-Policy. Follow only owned synthetic links to a test sink and inspect whether URLs reveal private state.
controls.pass: Types prevent unintended interpretation; sensitive URL data is minimized and not leaked by referrers. Browser capabilities are restricted to actual needs. COOP/COEP/CORP are evaluated where isolation is needed, not blindly enabled at the cost of trusted integrations.
controls.evidence: Response header matrix, capability rationale and synthetic referrer/network inspection.

controls.title: Validate redirect and return destinations
controls.applicability: Login return URLs, payment return pages, redirect endpoints or server-side forwards.
controls.verify: With owned local origins, test external, protocol-relative, encoded and near-match destination values. Verify both server/client redirects, their termination behavior and any forward to a protected handler.
controls.pass: Destinations are fixed, relative and safely resolved, or checked against a strict parsed allowlist. Untrusted values cannot send credentials/tokens to another origin or bypass authorization via an internal forward.
controls.evidence: Destination policy and negative test table; final resolved URLs and absence of leaked test tokens.

controls.title: Validate cross-window messages and sandbox untrusted embeds
controls.applicability: postMessage, embedded widgets, iframes or cross-window communication.
controls.verify: In a local fixture, send valid-schema messages from an untrusted origin/window and invalid-schema messages from the expected origin. Inspect exact origin/source checks, outbound targetOrigin, sandbox flags and whether messages reach code/HTML sinks.
controls.pass: Only expected origin and window/context can trigger authorized actions; schemas and action permissions are checked. Outgoing sensitive messages use a specific target origin. Untrusted embeds have least necessary sandbox privileges and messages remain data.
controls.evidence: Message-origin/schema test matrix, handler code locations and embed configuration.

controls.title: Prevent private cache leakage and cache-key confusion
controls.applicability: Browser, service-worker, CDN, proxy or application caching.
controls.verify: With synthetic accounts A and B, request the same personalized route and compare cached results. In an isolated cache, test path suffixes, relevant query/header variations and permission changes; inspect cache keys and service-worker fetch rules.
controls.pass: Private data is not reused across users/tenants, and cache policy/keying matches all response-varying inputs. Sensitive responses use suitable no-store/private policy; no-cache is not mistaken for no storage. Removed permissions and policy changes invalidate affected cached content.
controls.evidence: Two-account cache trace, key/rule configuration and stale-permission/path-variation results.

controls.title: Minimize browser storage and offline sensitive data
controls.applicability: localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, service workers, offline features or bearer-token storage.
controls.verify: Inspect browser storage for a synthetic account after login, logout and account switch. Review retention and script access to stored credentials; test offline/back navigation on a shared-device fixture without copying real data.
controls.pass: High-value credentials and sensitive records are not persisted in script-readable storage without an explicit reviewed need and mitigations. Logout/account switch clears relevant local state; offline caches cannot expose one account's data to another.
controls.evidence: Storage inventory with data classifications, lifecycle test results and justified retention limits.

controls.title: Limit client-delivered data and tracking exposure
controls.applicability: Client bundles, hydration/server-component payloads, source maps, analytics and replay tools.
controls.verify: Build the app locally and inspect browser-delivered artifacts and synthetic network traffic for server secrets, hidden/private fields, reset tokens and personal form values. Trace analytics/session-replay calls using a local sink or disabled external delivery.
controls.pass: Only intended public configuration and authorized data reach the browser. Secret-bearing modules remain server-only; source maps/debug details receive an exposure decision. Tracking is configured to minimize/redact sensitive content and does not collect authentication/payment secrets.
controls.evidence: Artifact/data-flow review, sanitized network trace, redaction settings and source-map publication rationale.

controls.title: Validate host and forwarded authority before building URLs
controls.applicability: Apps behind proxies, virtual hosts, caches, or generating absolute URLs such as reset and invitation links.
controls.verify: In isolated local/staging requests use a reserved .invalid host marker in Host, HTTP/2 :authority and forwarded-host/proto headers. Use a local mail sink for one synthetic reset/invitation. Inspect redirect/link generation, cache keys and virtual-host routing; never poison a shared production cache.
controls.pass: Unrecognized hosts are rejected or canonicalized safely. Only known proxies supply trusted forwarded metadata. Reset/invitation links and security decisions use configured trusted origins; hostile authority cannot redirect tokens, mix tenants, expose a default virtual host or contaminate another user cache entry.
controls.evidence: Proxy/allowed-host settings, bounded request/response pairs, synthetic mail-sink links and isolated cache/routing results.

controls.title: Enforce browser HTTPS with a reviewed HSTS rollout
controls.applicability: Browser-facing production domains using HTTPS; local-only non-TLS development needs a documented exclusion.
controls.verify: Inspect intended release headers and a few approved staging responses for HTTPS enforcement and Strict-Transport-Security. Review domain/subdomain inventory, certificate renewal and rollout/rollback plan; do not submit a domain for preload as part of the audit.
controls.pass: Browser-facing sensitive flows enforce HTTPS and the release configuration sends a deliberate HSTS policy over HTTPS. max-age and any includeSubDomains/preload choice match domain ownership, HTTPS coverage and operational recovery. Do not blindly enable preload or subdomain coverage; a pending HSTS deployment remains an explicit gap.
controls.evidence: Actual response headers, HTTP/HTTPS behavior, reviewed subdomain/certificate inventory and approved staged HSTS policy.

controls.title: Validate at every data boundary
controls.applicability: All inputs, including forms, imports, webhooks and stored integration data.
controls.verify: Review server schemas; send a small synthetic set with wrong types, duplicate keys, unexpected fields, Unicode edge cases and boundary lengths through each parser.
controls.pass: Canonicalization is consistent; required types, ranges, lengths and field allowlists are enforced before use. Client validation alone is insufficient.
controls.evidence: Schema/code locations plus expected versus actual rejection results.

controls.title: Prevent SQL and ORM query injection
controls.applicability: Relational queries, raw ORM expressions, reports and administrative filters.
controls.verify: Trace untrusted values, including previously stored values, to query construction; use harmless quote and sort-field fixtures against seeded records.
controls.pass: Values use bound parameters; dynamic identifiers and directions come from fixed choices; inputs cannot change query structure.
controls.evidence: Reviewed query paths and regression results showing only intended synthetic rows.

controls.title: Prevent NoSQL operator and query injection
controls.applicability: Document databases, search engines or user-controlled query objects.
controls.verify: Review driver calls; submit scalar-versus-object and operator-shaped fixtures against a tiny seeded dataset.
controls.pass: Typed scalar values and explicit query construction prevent injected operators or expressions; unknown fields are rejected.
controls.evidence: Query builder review and synthetic response comparisons.

controls.title: Prevent command and argument injection
controls.applicability: Conversion tools, shell/process calls, backups or utilities accepting input.
controls.verify: Trace process invocations; test punctuation and option-like strings using a stub executable that records arguments without side effects.
controls.pass: Shell interpolation is absent where avoidable; executable and arguments are constrained; input cannot add options, commands or output paths.
controls.evidence: Call-site inventory and recorded stub argument vectors.

controls.title: Keep data out of executable templates and expressions
controls.applicability: Server templates, rule engines, user-authored reports or dynamic code evaluation.
controls.verify: Review render/eval boundaries; pass harmless arithmetic-like text to ordinary fields. For intentional custom templates, test forbidden attribute access using inert objects in isolation.
controls.pass: Ordinary content remains data. Intentional template execution uses restricted data and capabilities plus process/resource isolation; a template sandbox alone is insufficient.
controls.evidence: Template configuration and bounded fixture outcomes, with allowed capabilities documented.

controls.title: Disable external XML resolution and unsafe expansion
controls.applicability: XML, SOAP, SVG, office-document or XML-backed import parsers.
controls.verify: Inspect the actual parser/version configuration; use tiny documents referencing a dedicated stub endpoint and a synthetic local fixture. Review expansion limits without generating a bomb.
controls.pass: External entities, DTD retrieval and unsafe transforms are disabled unless narrowly required; parser limits hold and no unauthorized read or request occurs.
controls.evidence: Parser settings, stub access log showing no fetch, and rejection results.

controls.title: Avoid unsafe object deserialization
controls.applicability: Cookies, queues, caches, imports or services deserializing externally influenced bytes.
controls.verify: Inventory serializers and polymorphic type settings; use invalid and unexpected-type fixtures. Review code instead of executing gadget chains.
controls.pass: Untrusted data cannot instantiate arbitrary classes or invoke code; schemas use constrained data types. BinaryFormatter and unsafe pickle-like formats are absent from untrusted boundaries.
controls.evidence: Serializer inventory, configuration and negative tests.

controls.title: Prevent prototype pollution
controls.applicability: JavaScript merges, nested query parsers or dynamic object-key assignment.
controls.verify: In isolated unit tests, submit reserved prototype-related keys through each merge/parser and inspect a fresh object's inherited properties.
controls.pass: Untrusted keys cannot alter prototypes, defaults, authorization flags or unrelated objects; safe maps and own-property checks are used appropriately.
controls.evidence: Parser/merge review and before/after object-state assertions.

controls.title: Encode reflected content for its output context
controls.applicability: Search, validation errors, previews and other reflected values.
controls.verify: Insert inert HTML, attribute and URL markers; inspect response and browser DOM in the local/staging app.
controls.pass: Untrusted values stay text or safe validated URLs in the actual context; escaping bypasses and dangerous template sinks are removed.
controls.evidence: Response/DOM evidence for representative contexts and sink review.

controls.title: Test stored XSS across roles and integrations
controls.applicability: CRM notes, contact forms, auction listings, bookings, messages and imported content.
controls.verify: Store a harmless local marker with markup metacharacters as one test user; view it as a separate test role in app, admin, CRM and notification previews.
controls.pass: Every rendering path preserves safe content boundaries; a low-privilege author cannot execute script in another role's session.
controls.evidence: Storage-to-render path inventory and two-role DOM results; use test notification sinks.

controls.title: Audit DOM sinks and client-side trust boundaries
controls.applicability: Client code consumes URL fragments, storage, postMessage, API data or third-party widgets.
controls.verify: Trace these sources to HTML, script and URL sinks; exercise inert markers and wrong-origin synthetic messages in a browser test.
controls.pass: Text APIs or appropriate sanitization protect DOM writes; message origin/source/schema are checked; input never becomes executable code.
controls.evidence: Source-to-sink review and local browser assertions.

controls.title: Sanitize intentionally rich content
controls.applicability: Rich text, Markdown with HTML, embedded content or customizable templates.
controls.verify: Test the maintained sanitizer with a small regression corpus covering event attributes, unsafe URL schemes and nested markup; inspect after all transforms.
controls.pass: Allowlisted content survives safely; dangerous elements/attributes/protocols are removed; later transforms do not restore unsafe markup. Regex stripping is insufficient.
controls.evidence: Sanitizer version/configuration and post-transform DOM checks.

controls.title: Prevent header, email and protocol injection
controls.applicability: Input influences HTTP headers, filenames in responses, email headers or mail commands.
controls.verify: Use newline/control-character fixtures with a local HTTP/email capture sink; inspect serialized messages.
controls.pass: Values cannot create extra headers, recipients, responses or protocol commands; framework APIs and explicit validation constrain structure.
controls.evidence: Captured synthetic messages and relevant header construction code.

controls.title: Make spreadsheet exports safe to open
controls.applicability: CSV, spreadsheet or tabular exports containing user data.
controls.verify: Export synthetic cells beginning with formula-like prefixes and separator/quote/newline variants; open and re-save in supported spreadsheet clients without external connections.
controls.pass: Untrusted cells remain text after supported open/save/reopen workflows; a documented safe export format is used where CSV mitigation is unreliable.
controls.evidence: Representative export files and supported-client validation results.

controls.title: Constrain LDAP, XPath and other query languages
controls.applicability: Directory searches, XPath/XML queries or custom expression languages.
controls.verify: Trace input to query APIs; use harmless syntax/metacharacter fixtures against a small test directory/document.
controls.pass: Parameterized or context-correct construction prevents input changing query operators or structure; allowlists constrain unavoidable dynamic syntax.
controls.evidence: Query-construction review and synthetic result comparisons.

controls.title: Enforce server-side file type policy
controls.applicability: Any upload, including direct-to-storage and batch workflows.
controls.verify: Submit small harmless extension/MIME/signature mismatches, mixed-case/double extensions and batch combinations through every upload path.
controls.pass: Business-approved formats are validated server-side using content-aware checks; client MIME or extension alone cannot approve a file.
controls.evidence: Type policy, validator code and allow/reject matrix.

controls.title: Contain SVG, HTML and other active uploads
controls.applicability: SVG/HTML or other browser-active documents can be uploaded or previewed.
controls.verify: Use synthetic active-content fixtures on local/staging only; inspect direct viewing, thumbnails, embeds and administrator previews.
controls.pass: Unneeded active formats are rejected; required formats use vetted sanitization or inert conversion and appropriate isolated serving. Untrusted active content cannot execute with application privileges.
controls.evidence: Upload/preview design, sanitizer settings and browser results for each serving mode.

controls.title: Isolate conversion, preview and scanning pipelines
controls.applicability: Image/PDF/office/media parsers, OCR, document previews or malware scanning.
controls.verify: Review worker privileges, outbound access and patch status; feed a tiny malformed-file corpus and simulate scanner timeout/unavailability.
controls.pass: Parsing is bounded and isolated; failures quarantine or reject files according to policy; no executable upload or privileged parser access is possible. Scan success alone is not a pass.
controls.evidence: Worker configuration, failure-path tests and parser/advisory inventory.

controls.title: Keep file paths within authorized storage
controls.applicability: File read/write/delete, downloads, imports or user-influenced filenames.
controls.verify: Use a temporary directory with synthetic inside/outside sentinel files; exercise encoded separators, absolute paths and symlinks through application functions.
controls.pass: Resolved paths remain within the intended root; traversal, links and race windows cannot read, overwrite or delete outside it; names are server assigned where practical.
controls.evidence: Sentinel assertions and canonical-path/open logic review.

controls.title: Bound archive extraction and decompression
controls.applicability: ZIP/TAR, compressed requests or archive imports.
controls.verify: Use tiny archives with parent paths, absolute paths and links; set very low test thresholds to verify member count, expanded-byte, nesting and time limits.
controls.pass: Extraction cannot escape its destination; limits apply to expanded content and links; partial failure leaves no executable or accessible residue.
controls.evidence: Archive fixtures, configured limits and filesystem assertions.

controls.title: Serve uploads with safe metadata and lifetime
controls.applicability: Uploaded or generated files are retrievable.
controls.verify: Inspect download responses, storage mappings and signed-link lifetimes using test files; test replaced/deleted files and unsafe original names.
controls.pass: Uploaded bytes are never executed as server code; content types and dispositions match policy; expired/deleted objects cannot remain unintentionally available; private access is also covered by authorization checks.
controls.evidence: Response headers, storage/retention configuration and lifecycle test results.

controls.title: Constrain REST methods, parsing and response shape
controls.applicability: REST/RPC endpoints, legacy routes or multiple content parsers.
controls.verify: Use a bounded matrix of unsupported methods, content types, duplicate parameters and malformed bodies; compare public response fields with the contract.
controls.pass: Only documented methods/formats work; ambiguity is rejected consistently; errors expose no internal data and responses contain only intended fields.
controls.evidence: Endpoint contract and request/response matrix.

controls.title: Bound GraphQL execution and schema exposure
controls.applicability: GraphQL endpoints, batching or subscriptions.
controls.verify: Against tiny fixtures, test depth, aliases, batch count, list size and query-cost limits with reduced thresholds; inspect resolver authorization and error/introspection policy.
controls.pass: Limits apply to total work, not just HTTP request count; resolvers enforce access; introspection/debug exposure matches policy without being treated as authorization.
controls.evidence: Schema/configuration and bounded query results including rejection before costly execution.

controls.title: Enforce WebSocket security throughout the connection
controls.applicability: WebSockets, live bidding, chat or subscriptions.
controls.verify: Use two test accounts and a few messages to check untrusted origins, expired/revoked sessions, cross-channel access, invalid messages and reduced frame/rate limits.
controls.pass: Origin/session checks and per-message authorization hold; schema, connection, buffer and rate bounds apply; revocation closes or disables existing sessions.
controls.evidence: Handshake/message traces, lifecycle assertions and limit settings.

controls.title: Restrict server-side fetch destinations
controls.applicability: URL previews, import-by-URL, image proxies, callbacks or any user-influenced outbound request.
controls.verify: Review URL parsing and egress policy; use injected DNS/HTTP stubs to represent private, loopback, link-local and IPv6 destinations without contacting real internal services or metadata.
controls.pass: Only intended schemes, hosts, ports and resolved destinations are reachable; internal/metadata access is denied unless specifically required and scoped.
controls.evidence: Destination policy and stub-based allow/deny tests.

controls.title: Revalidate redirects, DNS changes and fetch size
controls.applicability: Server-side fetches can redirect, resolve names or consume remote bodies.
controls.verify: Use a local mock resolver and HTTP server with redirect chains, address changes, slow responses and tiny configured body limits.
controls.pass: Every hop and connection obeys destination policy; credentials do not cross trust boundaries; redirects, time and response bytes are bounded.
controls.evidence: Mock trace and redirect/resolution/timeout assertions.

controls.title: Align proxy and backend HTTP interpretation
controls.applicability: Multiple HTTP parsers, reverse proxies, CDNs or protocol translation.
controls.verify: Review parser versions/settings and forwarding rules. Only in an explicitly isolated test stack, send a few ambiguous framing fixtures with no other users.
controls.pass: Ambiguous requests are rejected or normalized consistently; permissive parser modes are disabled; no extra backend request or response contamination occurs.
controls.evidence: Proxy/backend configuration, advisory review and isolated request-count assertions; otherwise mark dynamic test Blocked.

controls.title: Rate-limit sensitive and automatable workflows
controls.applicability: Login/recovery, invitations, contact forms, reservations, auctions and paid external calls.
controls.verify: Review per-account, tenant, destination and network limits; lower thresholds in staging and exceed each by one using test accounts and sink services.
controls.pass: Limits cannot be bypassed by alternate endpoints or forged proxy headers; responses and recovery are predictable; no real accounts are locked or users messaged.
controls.evidence: Limit policy, shared-counter configuration and low-volume tests.

controls.title: Bound queries, pagination and bulk operations
controls.applicability: Search, exports, reporting, nested filters, bulk updates or list APIs.
controls.verify: Inspect query plans on a small representative dataset; test missing/negative/huge page sizes and reduced limits for result count, offset, filters and batch length.
controls.pass: Server-enforced caps and deadlines bound work and output; user inputs cannot request unbounded queries or bypass limits through batch/nested forms.
controls.evidence: Query/limit review and boundary-test results with execution plans where useful.

controls.title: Bound CPU, memory, body sizes and deadlines
controls.applicability: All request handlers, especially regex, decompression and synchronous processing.
controls.verify: Inspect body/header limits, parser depth and operation deadlines; use reduced thresholds and short synthetic worst-case inputs under a strict local time budget.
controls.pass: Each expensive stage has effective bounds or isolation; timeout/cancellation releases resources; one request cannot monopolize the worker/event loop.
controls.evidence: Limit configuration and bounded timing/memory observations, not production load-test claims.

controls.title: Control outbound amplification and spending
controls.applicability: Email/SMS, AI, maps, payment-provider calls or fan-out services.
controls.verify: Replace providers with counters; submit one request triggering retries and controlled failures; inspect budget and per-destination quotas.
controls.pass: Fan-out, retry counts and total elapsed time are bounded; abuse cannot create unlimited billable work; alerts and kill switches have owners.
controls.evidence: Stub call counts, retry policy and configured budget/alert evidence.

controls.title: Bound asynchronous queues and failure recovery
controls.applicability: Background jobs, scheduled tasks, imports and event consumers.
controls.verify: With a tiny local queue, simulate a poison job and downstream timeout; observe retry, cancellation and dead-letter handling.
controls.pass: Queue depth, concurrency, retry attempts and job age are bounded; poisoned work cannot starve other tenants; cleanup and recovery paths are documented.
controls.evidence: Queue/worker settings and synthetic recovery trace.

controls.title: Treat prompts, retrieved content and tool output as untrusted
controls.applicability: LLM chat, RAG, agents or AI-assisted workflows.
controls.verify: Seed local documents/tool stubs with instructions that contradict the task; test a small direct/indirect injection set using synthetic data.
controls.pass: Application authorization and capability boundaries hold despite model behavior; external content cannot grant new permissions. Prompt wording or a detector alone is not a security boundary.
controls.evidence: Threat cases, model/version/settings and recorded tool-policy decisions.

controls.title: Validate AI output before rendering or execution
controls.applicability: Model output reaches HTML, SQL, shell, URLs, structured actions or business decisions.
controls.verify: Substitute deterministic model outputs containing inert markup, unexpected fields and unsafe action requests; run local integration tests.
controls.pass: Outputs receive the same validation, encoding and parameterization as other untrusted input; generated code/actions cannot execute solely because the model proposed them.
controls.evidence: Output schema/sink review and deterministic negative tests.

controls.title: Constrain AI tools and require meaningful approval
controls.applicability: Agents can send messages, alter records, spend money, run code or access external tools.
controls.verify: Use mock tools and a test principal; try unauthorized objects/actions, changed arguments after approval and a replay of an approved action.
controls.pass: Server-side policy constrains every tool call to the actor and task; consequential actions require required scoped approval; approval binds concrete arguments and cannot be reused improperly.
controls.evidence: Tool allowlist, policy checks and blocked-call/approval-binding tests.

controls.title: Protect retrieval, memory and model-bound data
controls.applicability: RAG indexes, conversation memory, uploaded documents or external model providers.
controls.verify: Use synthetic tenant-tagged documents and canary values; query as separate test users and inspect retrieval filters, caches, prompts and retention settings.
controls.pass: Unauthorized data never enters the model context or shared memory; sensitive fields are minimized; provider use and retention match approved policy.
controls.evidence: Retrieval/cache isolation tests and documented data destinations/retention.

controls.title: Cap AI costs, loops and persistent influence
controls.applicability: AI inference, recursive tool calls, memory updates or user-contributed retrieval content.
controls.verify: With a deterministic model stub, simulate tool loops, large outputs and attempted persistent instruction storage; lower quotas to exercise cutoff.
controls.pass: Token/time/call/spend budgets terminate work; memory/content promotion has provenance and review appropriate to impact; no untrusted instruction becomes privileged policy.
controls.evidence: Budget/cancellation results and memory ingestion/provenance review.

controls.title: Review Next.js server/client and action boundaries
controls.applicability: Next.js App/Pages Router or React Server Components.
controls.verify: Inspect Server Actions, Route Handlers/API routes, DAL, client props and caches; call actions directly with synthetic users; inspect built client artifacts for synthetic secret markers.
controls.pass: Each server entry enforces validation and access independently; server-only data stays server-side; serialized props and shared caches expose only permitted fields. Middleware/page checks alone are insufficient.
controls.evidence: Entry-point matrix, build/response inspection and direct-call regression results; check current Next.js/React advisories for deployed versions.

controls.title: Harden Node.js runtime and HTTP server settings
controls.applicability: Node.js applications, custom servers or worker processes.
controls.verify: Inspect start flags, inspector exposure, HTTP timeout/limit settings, unsafe parser options and synchronous hotspots; verify small isolated boundary fixtures.
controls.pass: Debug interfaces are not externally reachable; strict parsing and deadlines are effective; untrusted input cannot invoke eval, unsafe native operations or unrestricted process execution.
controls.evidence: Runtime/configuration inventory and local boundary results; verify supported runtime and current official advisories.

controls.title: Review Python runtime and framework deployment hazards
controls.applicability: Python web apps, workers and framework extensions.
controls.verify: Inventory pickle/eval/subprocess/XML/archive use; inspect production server/debug settings and trusted host/proxy configuration. Run the installed framework's deployment checks where provided.
controls.pass: Unsafe serialization/execution boundaries are removed or constrained; development server/debugger is absent; relevant deployment warnings are resolved or recorded. Match Django guidance only when Django applies.
controls.evidence: Runtime/framework versions, call-site review, deployment-check output and configuration evidence; refresh relevant advisories.

controls.title: Review ASP.NET Core pipeline and proxy trust
controls.applicability: ASP.NET Core/.NET web apps and APIs.
controls.verify: Inspect middleware order, endpoint coverage, environment/error configuration and known proxy/network settings; send synthetic spoofed forwarding headers through the local proxy chain.
controls.pass: Security middleware covers intended endpoints; untrusted headers cannot change trusted client/host/scheme decisions; development exception data is absent; unsafe serializers are removed.
controls.evidence: Pipeline/proxy configuration, synthetic header tests and deployed-version advisory review.

controls.title: Bind price, amount, currency and order on the server
controls.applicability: Any checkout, invoice, donation, paid booking or auction settlement.
controls.verify: With provider test mode and two synthetic orders, alter client price, discount, quantity, currency and order reference; present a valid event for the other order. Inspect minor-unit and rounding calculations.
controls.pass: The server derives payable totals from approved records and verifies provider account, environment, transaction, amount, currency and order binding before payment or fulfillment state changes.
controls.evidence: Redacted test requests, expected totals, provider test IDs and before/after order records.

controls.title: A return page never proves payment
controls.applicability: Payment redirects, success pages and CRM paid-state synchronization.
controls.verify: Visit the success URL directly and after cancellation, decline, incomplete authentication and pending asynchronous payment. Compare the UI, local order and synthetic CRM record with authoritative provider state.
controls.pass: No redirect parameter or browser callback alone marks an order paid. Pending/failed orders remain visibly unpaid; fulfillment and CRM paid status require verified server-side payment state.
controls.evidence: State matrix for success/pending/failure, redacted test IDs, CRM stub records and relevant server code.

controls.title: Verify webhook signatures and replay freshness
controls.applicability: Incoming payment or other security-sensitive provider webhooks.
controls.verify: Locally sign synthetic fixtures with a test secret. Check missing/invalid signature, changed raw bytes, expired timestamp, wrong endpoint secret and wrong environment; inspect the provider-supported verification call.
controls.pass: Verification uses the provider's required raw payload and algorithm before processing; rejects forged/stale events using documented tolerance and reliable time. Secret rollover follows provider rules; IP allowlists alone are insufficient.
controls.evidence: Verifier configuration without secrets and negative/positive fixture results.

controls.title: Payment and fulfillment are idempotent
controls.applicability: Payment creation, refunds, webhook handling and fulfillment.
controls.verify: Submit one synthetic payment request twice with its stable operation key; deliver the same verified event twice and process two copies concurrently in a local transaction test.
controls.pass: One business operation creates at most one payment/refund/fulfillment. Durable unique constraints and atomic claim/commit enforce deduplication; provider idempotency keys are bound to the intended operation and parameters.
controls.evidence: Duplicate/concurrent test output and database constraints, transaction or idempotency-store design.

controls.title: Handle delayed, reordered and failed delivery
controls.applicability: Asynchronous payment events and background workers.
controls.verify: Use a local queue/provider stub to reorder valid events, delay success, fail processing before/after durable commit, and replay after restart. Simulate a temporary provider lookup failure.
controls.pass: State transitions preserve business invariants; stale events cannot revert final state incorrectly. Acknowledgment occurs only after durable acceptance, retries are bounded, failures are visible and uncertain payments stay unconfirmed.
controls.evidence: Transition table, restart/replay results and dead-letter/reconciliation runbook.

controls.title: Reconcile settlement, refunds and disputes
controls.applicability: Captured payments, partial refunds, subscriptions, chargebacks or CRM accounting.
controls.verify: Use test-mode fixtures for authorization versus capture, partial/full refund, duplicate refund and dispute; introduce one synthetic mismatch between provider, local ledger and CRM.
controls.pass: Financial states remain distinct and correctly mapped. Refund totals cannot exceed captured funds; reconciliation finds the mismatch and routes it to a named owner without inventing payment success.
controls.evidence: Ledger/state mapping, synthetic reconciliation report and refund boundary tests.

controls.title: Limit payment data and separate test/live configuration
controls.applicability: Any card or payment provider integration.
controls.verify: Inspect the payment data flow and release configuration without reading secrets; search synthetic logs and browser storage for test card fields, client secrets and payment tokens. Check test/live key and webhook endpoint pairing.
controls.pass: Hosted/tokenized collection minimizes card data exposure; prohibited sensitive card data is not retained. Environment separation is explicit and payment-compliance scope is reviewed with the provider/acquirer; this checklist does not certify compliance.
controls.evidence: Redacted configuration inventory, data-flow diagram and synthetic log/storage inspection.

controls.title: Authorize financial actions independently
controls.applicability: Refunds, manual paid overrides, payout changes and administrative settlement.
controls.verify: With synthetic customer, support and finance roles, invoke financial endpoints directly and change order/customer IDs. Review step-up or dual approval for high-impact operations and trace who approved an override.
controls.pass: Only explicitly permitted actors can perform each financial action on the intended order; significant amount/destination changes invalidate prior approval. Overrides preserve an attributable reason and cannot silently bypass payment evidence.
controls.evidence: Role/action test matrix, approval-binding checks and redacted audit trail.

controls.title: Prevent booking and inventory races
controls.applicability: Limited-capacity bookings, inventory reservations or ticket sales.
controls.verify: Run a bounded local test with two transactions competing for the last synthetic slot/item, including hold expiration and cancellation between check and commit; use barriers rather than load generation.
controls.pass: Database-level transactions, constraints or equivalent serialization preserve capacity. At most one winner receives confirmation; retries and expired holds cannot oversell or lose inventory.
controls.evidence: Concurrency test trace, invariant assertions and transaction/constraint definitions.

controls.title: Enforce auction timing and winner invariants
controls.applicability: Online auctions or competitive bidding.
controls.verify: With synthetic bids and a controlled clock, submit bids below the minimum, after close, from an ineligible bidder and concurrently near closing; replay a prior bid and run settlement twice.
controls.pass: Server time and atomic rules determine valid bids, extensions, closing and one winner. Clients cannot alter reserve/minimum/close state, see restricted bid data, or trigger duplicate settlement.
controls.evidence: Boundary/concurrency cases, winner calculation and settlement ledger assertions.

controls.title: Protect value-bearing quantities and entitlements
controls.applicability: Coupons, credits, reward points, trials, quotas or downloadable entitlements.
controls.verify: Use isolated fixtures with zero/negative/very large quantities, repeated coupon redemption, parallel credit spending and client-supplied entitlement flags. Inspect expiry and tenant/account binding.
controls.pass: Server-derived values satisfy documented numeric and business bounds; single-use benefits and balances cannot be reused or spent twice; entitlements require the authoritative qualifying state.
controls.evidence: Value invariants, boundary results and unique/redemption constraints.

controls.title: Reject skipped, replayed and invalid workflow steps
controls.applicability: Multi-step approvals, onboarding, booking changes or business transactions.
controls.verify: Call later steps directly, replay a completed step and modify material data after approval using synthetic records. Inspect cancellation, timeout and recovery paths.
controls.pass: An explicit server-side state machine authorizes each transition against current data and actor. Approvals are bound to the approved data, and invalid transitions have no partial side effects.
controls.evidence: State diagram, denied-transition results and atomicity checks.

controls.title: Keep cross-system side effects consistent
controls.applicability: A database change also publishes a job, sends a notification or updates CRM.
controls.verify: Inject local stub failures before and after the database commit, queue publication and remote acknowledgment; restart workers and replay the operation once.
controls.pass: Durable outbox/inbox, compensation or an equivalent documented design prevents lost or duplicate business effects. A remote failure is not reported as successful completion; repair is observable and idempotent.
controls.evidence: Fault-injection traces, outbox/retry design and recovery demonstration.

controls.title: Constrain CRM and Odoo service accounts
controls.applicability: CRM/Odoo connectors or custom Odoo modules.
controls.verify: Review connector scopes, Odoo ACLs, record rules, company context and each sudo/public RPC method. With two synthetic companies and a low-privilege connector account, attempt an unrelated record/action.
controls.pass: Connector privileges are limited to required models/actions/companies; public methods validate untrusted arguments and authorization. sudo cannot bypass the caller's intended scope; secrets never reach the browser.
controls.evidence: Service-account permission matrix, redacted ACL/rule definitions and denied cross-company tests.

controls.title: Treat provider responses as untrusted data
controls.applicability: Third-party APIs, CRM imports, enrichment, shipping or other external data.
controls.verify: Configure a local stub to return malformed, oversized and unexpected fields, script-like text, unapproved redirect URLs and a mismatched object ID. Review downstream rendering and database writes.
controls.pass: Schema, size, identity and business checks precede use; third-party text receives the same injection defenses as user input. Redirects and destinations are restricted; external data cannot confer local authorization.
controls.evidence: Stub fixtures, validation failures and consumer/renderer code references.

controls.title: Bound failures, timeouts and retries
controls.applicability: Outbound integrations and asynchronous jobs.
controls.verify: Make an isolated stub time out, return rate limits, fail TLS and provide partial results. Inspect request deadlines, connection pools, retry/backoff budgets, cancellation and circuit-breaking behavior.
controls.pass: Failures fail safely without granting access or claiming success. Time, retry count, queue growth and response bytes are bounded; retries of writes are idempotent and alerts identify exhausted work.
controls.evidence: Failure-case results, configured budgets and retry/dead-letter evidence.

controls.title: Review third-party browser code and consent
controls.applicability: Analytics, tag managers, chat widgets, payment scripts or embedded vendors.
controls.verify: Inventory scripts and iframes on sensitive pages using synthetic sessions; record data sent and vendor permissions. Review version integrity/pinning where supported, sandbox boundaries and change ownership.
controls.pass: Each vendor has an owner, purpose and minimum data access. Sensitive pages exclude unnecessary scripts; integrity/CSP/sandbox controls fit the integration, and consent/data-sharing requirements are documented.
controls.evidence: Third-party inventory, synthetic network record and reviewed script/sandbox policy.

controls.title: Prevent notification misuse and recipient manipulation
controls.applicability: Contact forms, email/SMS delivery, invitations or transactional messages.
controls.verify: Use an email/SMS sink to alter recipient, reply-to, template variables and header-like input; exercise one duplicate event and one unauthorized bulk-send request.
controls.pass: Recipients and templates follow server-side authorization and validation; messages do not expose other users' data or inject headers/HTML. Send budgets, deduplication and unsubscribe/consent rules fit the message type.
controls.evidence: Sink messages, denied recipient/bulk cases and sender budget configuration.

controls.title: Find secrets in code, artifacts and client bundles
controls.applicability: All builds, repositories, configuration and deployment artifacts.
controls.verify: Run a local secret scan with redacted output over the intended release and available authorized history; inspect browser bundles, source maps, images, sample configs and CI artifacts. Verify scanner operation with a synthetic canary.
controls.pass: No real credential, private key or reusable signing secret is exposed. Suspected values are confirmed by ownership/configuration evidence without using them; exposed credentials are revoked/rotated, not merely deleted.
controls.evidence: Scan scope/tool version, canary result, redacted findings and rotation references.

controls.title: Control secret access, rotation and emergency revocation
controls.applicability: Runtime/CI credentials, webhook secrets, signing and encryption keys.
controls.verify: Inspect secret-store IAM and delivery paths; rehearse rotation/revocation with a disposable local or staging credential, including worker refresh and rollback. Check departed-user and unused-secret access.
controls.pass: Only required workloads/operators can retrieve secrets. Rotation and revocation work within the documented window; no fallback uses hardcoded secrets and old credentials cease working after the planned overlap.
controls.evidence: Redacted access policy, rotation timing/result and ownership/expiry inventory.

controls.title: Use supported cryptography and protect keys separately
controls.applicability: Sensitive data encryption, signatures or custom token generation.
controls.verify: Review algorithms, libraries, authenticated encryption, key origin, nonce generation and storage separation; use test keys to alter ciphertext/tag and verify rejection. Inspect KMS grants and key-backup recovery design.
controls.pass: Supported libraries and approved algorithms match the threat model; integrity checks reject tampering, nonces are not reused, and data readers cannot automatically access encryption keys. No custom cryptographic protocol is assumed safe.
controls.evidence: Algorithm/key inventory without material, tamper-test result and KMS/storage permissions.

controls.title: Validate TLS across public and internal trust boundaries
controls.applicability: HTTPS endpoints, service-to-service, database, webhook and provider connections.
controls.verify: Review edge/origin/client TLS settings and perform a few handshakes against approved staging endpoints. Use a local invalid/expired/wrong-host certificate to check outbound rejection and inspect renewal monitoring. Check HTTP-to-HTTPS enforcement, mixed-content requests and HTTPS links in synthetic login/reset/payment flows without transmitting real credentials over HTTP.
controls.pass: Supported TLS configuration uses TLS 1.3 or justified TLS 1.2; deprecated SSL/TLS and weak suites are disabled. Certificate chain and hostname are validated, sensitive hops are encrypted and expiry alerts have an owner. Sensitive endpoints and clients require HTTPS with no HTTP downgrade or mixed active content; HTTP requests cannot process credentials or sensitive actions.
controls.evidence: Staging handshake report, client rejection tests and redacted edge/origin/renewal settings.

controls.title: Use unpredictable security tokens and safe comparisons
controls.applicability: Reset/invitation/API tokens, signatures and one-time capabilities.
controls.verify: Inspect randomness and token construction; verify use of the platform CSPRNG, sufficient entropy for documented guessing budgets, bounded expiry and constant-time MAC/token comparison where relevant. Test with synthetic tokens.
controls.pass: Security capabilities are not derived from time, counters, ordinary random functions or predictable IDs. Confidential token material is protected at rest and validation does not introduce avoidable timing leakage.
controls.evidence: Token design/entropy calculation, library calls and synthetic expired/altered-token results.

controls.title: Inventory exact deployed dependencies and advisories
controls.applicability: Every release, including frameworks, runtime, OS/base image, plugins and transitive packages.
controls.verify: Generate a release SBOM/lockfile inventory; query current vendor advisories and ecosystem scanners for the exact versions of Next.js/React, Node, Python/frameworks, .NET, Odoo and AWS components actually used. Record date and advisory coverage.
controls.pass: Versions are supported and applicable critical/high advisories are fixed and retested. Reachability and compensating controls are evidenced; a clean scanner result or old checklist is not proof of absence.
controls.evidence: Release digest/SBOM, dated advisory URLs, scanner versions and triage/fix evidence.

controls.title: Protect package resolution and installation
controls.applicability: npm, pip, NuGet, container and other dependency installation.
controls.verify: Inspect registry configuration, private-package namespaces, lockfiles/hashes and install hooks. Rebuild in an isolated runner with the approved registry configuration; review dependency changes before executing untrusted code.
controls.pass: Resolution is deterministic enough to reproduce the release and prevents private-name fallback to untrusted registries. Packages/actions are verified and pinned appropriately; installation hooks do not receive unnecessary secrets.
controls.evidence: Registry/lockfile review, dependency diff and isolated build provenance.

controls.title: Isolate untrusted CI input and pull requests
controls.applicability: CI jobs execute repository content, event data or third-party actions.
controls.verify: Review fork PR and privileged workflow paths, interpolated event fields, reusable workflows and cache/artifact consumption; use a benign synthetic PR title to test argument handling in a disposable workflow.
controls.pass: Untrusted code/metadata cannot execute with deployment secrets or writable privileged tokens. Inputs are passed as data, reviewed actions are pinned to immutable revisions, and shared runner/cache trust boundaries are enforced.
controls.evidence: Workflow data-flow review, token permissions and benign injection fixture result.

controls.title: Restrict deployment credentials and federation
