controls.applicability: CI/CD can modify production or assume cloud roles.
controls.verify: Inspect OIDC issuer/audience/subject conditions or scoped deployment credentials. Evaluate an unapproved repository, branch and environment against the trust policy without requesting real privileged tokens.
controls.pass: Only the intended repository/workflow/environment can assume the minimum deployment role; short-lived federation is preferred. Production approvals and environment protections cannot be bypassed by untrusted branches.
controls.evidence: Redacted trust/role policy and policy-simulation or isolated denial results.

controls.title: Deploy the reviewed artifact with protected changes
controls.applicability: Build, promotion and production configuration changes.
controls.verify: Trace the reviewed commit to artifact digest, provenance and deployment record; inspect branch/tag/environment protections and require review of application, IaC and workflow changes. Compare staging and release configuration.
controls.pass: The deployed artifact is identifiable and derives from the approved source/build; substitutions and unreviewed privileged changes are prevented. Security-relevant configuration differences are reviewed and rollback targets are retained.
controls.evidence: Commit-to-digest deployment chain, protection settings and configuration diff.

controls.title: Harden container and build runtime boundaries
controls.applicability: Container images, self-hosted runners or containerized apps.
controls.verify: Inspect Dockerfiles/manifests for root, privileged mode, capabilities, host/socket mounts, writable rootfs and limits; inspect final image layers for secrets and unneeded tools without running unknown images with host privileges.
controls.pass: Runtime privileges, writable paths and resource budgets are minimal; no unnecessary daemon socket/host access exists. Images and hosts are patched, and build-only dependencies/secrets are absent from runtime layers.
controls.evidence: Image digest/scan, manifest settings and layer inspection summary.

controls.title: Separate human and workload IAM permissions
controls.applicability: AWS accounts or equivalent cloud resources.
controls.verify: Review human federation/MFA, root-account protection, workload roles, trust policies and resource conditions; evaluate representative denied actions with a policy simulator or disposable test role.
controls.pass: Humans use attributable identities with MFA; workloads use scoped roles/temporary credentials where supported. Wildcard/admin and cross-account grants have explicit justification and unused permissions are removed.
controls.evidence: Redacted IAM/trust inventory and allowed/denied simulation results.

controls.title: Keep private storage private
controls.applicability: S3/object storage containing uploads, exports, backups or private application data.
controls.verify: Inspect effective account/bucket/access-point policies, ACL ownership and public-access settings. For an authorized synthetic object, verify anonymous listing/read/write denial and the intended authenticated access path.
controls.pass: Private storage is not publicly listable, readable or writable; public assets are deliberately separated. Encryption and retention are configured, and policy analysis includes resource and identity grants.
controls.evidence: Redacted effective policies, analyzer findings and synthetic access tests.

controls.title: Constrain signed object URLs
controls.applicability: Presigned upload/download URLs or signed CDN capabilities.
controls.verify: With disposable objects, request another user's key, change method/key, reuse an upload URL and check expiry. Inspect content/size constraints and post-upload validation; do not include signed URLs in audit evidence.
controls.pass: Signing requires object/action authorization, binds a narrow key/method and short appropriate lifetime, and avoids unintended overwrite. Reuse semantics are understood; one-time use is enforced separately if required.
controls.evidence: Redacted signing code, authorization/expiry tests and object-key policy.

controls.title: Evaluate actual network reachability
controls.applicability: Servers, containers, databases, admin tools or internal applications.
controls.verify: Review listeners, host/container port mappings, security groups, routes and IPv4/IPv6 rules. Use configuration analysis and only explicitly scoped staging connection checks for intended and forbidden paths.
controls.pass: Only intended services and clients have reachability, with authentication where required. Binding to 0.0.0.0 alone is not a finding; unintended exposure requires evidence of a reachable, insufficiently protected service.
controls.evidence: Reachability diagram, effective network policies and bounded connection results.

controls.title: Prevent edge and origin policy bypass
controls.applicability: CDN/WAF/reverse-proxy fronting an origin or load balancer.
controls.verify: Inspect origin ingress and edge-to-origin authentication. On scoped staging hosts, compare access through the edge and the documented direct-origin path, including spoofed client-supplied forwarding or origin headers.
controls.pass: Required edge controls cannot be bypassed through origin DNS/IP or alternate listeners. Private origins or properly protected origin authentication enforce the design; forwarded client identity is trusted only from approved proxies.
controls.evidence: Origin policy, architecture and staging edge/direct-path denial results.

controls.title: Restrict metadata and workload credential exposure
controls.applicability: EC2 or other compute with a metadata/credential endpoint.
controls.verify: Inspect metadata-service and workload identity settings plus application egress boundaries. Use only a local metadata stub to exercise SSRF paths; never retrieve real metadata credentials.
controls.pass: EC2 uses required IMDSv2 with appropriate hop/network settings or disables unused metadata. Workload roles are least privilege, and untrusted fetches cannot access credential endpoints; IMDSv2 is defense in depth, not an SSRF fix.
controls.evidence: Metadata options, role policy and local stub denial tests.

controls.title: Protect databases, queues and caches
controls.applicability: Managed or self-hosted databases, message brokers, caches and search stores.
controls.verify: Review network access, authenticated clients, TLS, application database grants and backup/snapshot sharing. With isolated fixtures, check that an application identity cannot administer the service or read another tenant's protected store.
controls.pass: Data services lack unintended public access, require scoped authenticated connections and protected transport, and separate administrative privileges. Snapshots/exports inherit the intended confidentiality boundary.
controls.evidence: Redacted grants/network policy, connection settings and denied privilege tests.

controls.title: Detect cloud security changes and preserve audit events
controls.applicability: AWS hosting or equivalent cloud management plane.
controls.verify: Review CloudTrail/analogous event coverage, protected destinations, integrity checks, retention and alerts for IAM, storage and logging changes. Replay a synthetic event into a test alert route.
controls.pass: Required regions/accounts and relevant management/data events are covered; application operators cannot erase the audit trail casually. Alert delivery and ownership are demonstrated without exposing sensitive log contents.
controls.evidence: Event coverage inventory, protected log policy and synthetic alert receipt.

controls.title: Isolate environments and remove abandoned exposure
controls.applicability: Production, staging, preview deployments, temporary resources and DNS.
controls.verify: Compare account/network/secret/data separation; inspect IaC and DNS inventory for orphaned endpoints, preview access and debug/admin tools. Validate ownership from configuration, without claiming third-party resources.
controls.pass: Nonproduction cannot access production secrets or personal data without explicit controls; previews require appropriate access. Retired endpoints/DNS and development interfaces are removed or protected with named owners.
controls.evidence: Environment access matrix, resource/DNS inventory and reviewed release configuration.

controls.title: Keep secrets and personal data out of logs
controls.applicability: Application, proxy, analytics, APM, error, CI and third-party logging.
controls.verify: Exercise synthetic login, recovery, payment and contact flows with identifiable canary values; inspect each permitted sink for bodies, headers, query strings and stack traces. Do not collect real secrets to prove leakage.
controls.pass: Passwords, session/reset tokens, payment credentials and unnecessary personal content are excluded or appropriately redacted before collection; retention and reader access match sensitivity.
controls.evidence: Canary search results by sink and redaction/access/retention settings.

controls.title: Create useful tamper-resistant security events
controls.applicability: Authentication, authorization, administrative or financial state changes.
controls.verify: Generate synthetic denial and privileged-change events; include newline/control characters in benign labels. Inspect correlation IDs, actor/object/action/outcome, time synchronization and log access; simulate sink failure locally.
controls.pass: Events support investigation without disclosing secrets. Untrusted text cannot forge entries or execute in viewers; access/integrity controls protect records and logging failure follows a documented safe behavior.
controls.evidence: Redacted event samples, injection fixture result, time/sink-failure test and permissions.

controls.title: Enforce data minimization, retention and deletion
controls.applicability: Personal, confidential or regulated data including contact/booking records.
controls.verify: Map each collected field to purpose, destination and retention; use a synthetic account to verify export/deletion behavior in primary storage, indexes, CRM and queued jobs. Review backup expiry and legal-hold handling with the owner.
controls.pass: Unnecessary data is not collected or shared; authorized requests and scheduled retention operate across copies, with documented backup/hold limitations. Applicable privacy obligations are owner-reviewed, not inferred as legal compliance.
controls.evidence: Data inventory, synthetic lifecycle results and approved retention/processor record.

controls.title: Protect recoverable backups
controls.applicability: Persistent business data, configuration and required key material.
controls.verify: Inspect backup coverage, encryption, restore roles, retention and deletion protection. Use policy analysis or disposable fixtures to check ordinary application credentials cannot delete every recovery copy; do not enable irreversible locks during an audit.
controls.pass: Backups cover required data/configuration and remain recoverable under the threat model; separate access and retention controls reduce ransomware/deletion risk. Key dependencies and ongoing costs are understood.
controls.evidence: Backup inventory, access/retention review and protected-copy evidence.

controls.title: Demonstrate isolated restore and recovery objectives
controls.applicability: Applications with persistent data or availability commitments.
controls.verify: Restore a synthetic backup into an isolated environment without overwriting production; validate record integrity, authentication, integrations disabled by default and a core business transaction. Measure recovery time and recoverable data age.
controls.pass: Restore works end to end within approved RTO/RPO; key/configuration dependencies are available, restored data stays private, and teardown follows the approved test plan.
controls.evidence: Restore run record, integrity/business assertions, measured RTO/RPO and cleanup record.

controls.title: Exercise incident detection and response
controls.applicability: All production services.
controls.verify: Run a tabletop for account takeover, exposed secret, stored XSS/data exposure and payment mismatch; route a synthetic alert to the test channel and walk containment, evidence preservation, communication and recovery.
controls.pass: Named responders can recognize, escalate and contain each scenario, revoke credentials/sessions and preserve needed evidence. Contacts, authority and notification obligations are current; simulation does not message real customers.
controls.evidence: Tabletop record, tested alert path, owner/on-call details and dated response playbooks.

controls.title: Prove safe rollback and security retest
controls.applicability: Releases, schema migrations and security fixes.
controls.verify: Rehearse rollback on a staging copy, including backward-compatible migrations and queued jobs; rerun the original negative test and one adjacent abuse case for each security fix. Verify the release commit/configuration matches the tested one.
controls.pass: Rollback restores a coherent supported state without silently reintroducing a known critical/high flaw. Findings close only after evidence-based retest; changed security boundaries reopen affected controls.
controls.evidence: Rollback/migration record, fix commit, original reproduction and dated retest evidence.
